newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Pension Plan 1997 contributions up 0.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Pension Plan 1997 contributions up 0.25 pct.

text.p: Contributions to the state-run Canada Pension Plan (CPP) will increase by 0.25 percentage points in 1997 to 5.85 percent of earnings from 5.6 percent this year, the Finance Department said on Monday.
The increase in contributions will be automatic and is in line with the 25-year schedule of contributions adopted in 1991 after an agreement was reached between Ottawa and the provincial governments.
The Finance Department said the contribution level may be raised further sometime in 1997 if a new federal-provincial agreement is reached in the near future.
Federal and provincial finance ministers have been negotiating for about a year on ways to prevent the CPP from running out of money.

A 1995 federal report warned the CPP could run out of funds by 2015 if currently agreed contribution rates and benefits are not changed. Several rounds of talks between Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin and his provincial counterparts have failed to produce a deal on channging the CPP.
Rescue proposals for the plan include raising contributions, cutting benefits and increasing the retirement age for Canadians. There have also been suggestions that CPP management be privatized.

If a deal is reached allowing an increase in CPP contributions in 1997, the increase will be collected when that year's tax returns are filed, the Finance Department said. ((Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau, 613-235-6745))
